name: Price Action
description: A method of analyzing market movement by studying price behavior and chart patterns.

name: Support and Resistance
description: Identifies important price areas where buying or selling pressure may appear.

name: Breakout Trading
description: Looks for price to move beyond an established support or resistance level.

name: Trend Following
description: Attempts to participate in an established market trend rather than predict reversals.

name: Swing Trading
description: Holds positions for several days or weeks to capture larger price movements.

name: Day Trading
description: Opens and closes trades within the same trading day.

name: Scalping
description: Uses short-term market movements to seek small price gains.

name: Moving Average Strategy
description: Uses moving averages to identify trends and potential changes in market direction.

name: Fibonacci Retracement
description: Uses Fibonacci levels to identify potential areas where price may retrace.

name: Fair Value Gap
description: Identifies areas of inefficient price movement that may later be revisited.

name: Liquidity Trading
description: Studies areas where significant concentrations of orders may exist around market highs and lows.

name: Order Blocks
description: Analyzes areas associated with significant institutional buying or selling activity.

name: Break of Structure
description: Uses changes in swing highs and lows to identify potential changes in market structure.

name: Candle Range Theory
description: Studies the relationship between candle ranges, liquidity, and subsequent price movement.

name: Risk-to-Reward Planning
description: Compares the potential reward of a trade with the amount being risked.

name: Position Sizing
description: Determines an appropriate trade size based on account balance, stop loss, and risk percentage.

name: Stop Loss Management
description: Uses predefined exit levels to help limit potential losses on a trade.

name: Multi-Timeframe Analysis
description: Combines multiple chart timeframes to build a broader view of market direction.
